docs.title: Docker Workflow Steps
docs.text: The Docker plugin exposes reusable public workflow steps through DockerPlugin.get_steps().

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: Step Group Used by built-in workflows select_service_group Compose docker-up select_services_to_stop Compose docker-down compose_up Compose docker-up compose_down Compose docker-down compose_status Compose docker-up, docker-down, docker-status build_push_images Build docker-build-push disk_usage Prune docker-prune select_prune_targets Prune docker-prune prune_resources Prune docker-prune select_containers_to_remove Containers docker-clean-containers remove_containers Containers docker-clean-containers

docs.title: Compose
docs.text:
Use these steps to resolve which services to operate on and drive the compose lifecycle.

  • select_service_group: let the user pick a project-configured service_groups entry (or "All services"), saving docker_services to the workflow context
  • select_services_to_stop: checkbox list of every compose service, all checked by default; unchecking one keeps it running. If everything stays checked, resolves to a full docker compose down; otherwise stops just the checked subset. Exits early (nothing to do) if the user unchecks everything.
  • compose_up: start the services in docker_services (all services if absent/empty)
  • compose_down: stop the services in docker_services (the whole project if absent/empty)
  • compose_status: show a table of service state/status/health for docker_services (all services if absent/empty), saving docker_compose_status to the workflow context. With no prior step setting docker_services, it reports on every service - this is what powers the standalone docker-status workflow.

docs.title: Build
docs.text:
Use this step to build (and push, per target config) configured Docker images.

  • build_push_images: build every configured build_targets entry, or a single one when build_target_name is set in the workflow context, saving docker_build_results to the workflow context. Streams docker buildx build output into a live, read-only text area per target (mouse-selectable and copyable) instead of a plain spinner.

docs.title: Prune
docs.text:
Use these steps to inspect and reclaim host-wide Docker disk usage. Unlike the Compose steps above, these are not scoped to this project's compose file - they report on the whole Docker host.

  • disk_usage: show a table of Docker's disk usage breakdown (images, containers, local volumes, build cache) via docker system df, saving docker_disk_usage to the workflow context
  • select_prune_targets: checkbox list of resource categories (stopped containers, dangling images, build cache, unused volumes), nothing checked by default since pruning is destructive. Exits early if nothing is selected. Note Docker itself refuses to remove a volume still attached to any container, so volumes never touches an in-use volume.
  • prune_resources: run docker ... prune for each target in prune_targets, saving docker_prune_results to the workflow context

docs.title: Containers
docs.text:
Use these steps to inspect and clean up containers across the whole host, not just this project.

  • select_containers_to_remove: list every container on the host (running and stopped) for context, then offer a checkbox list of the stopped ones for removal, nothing checked by default. Exits early if there are no stopped containers, or if nothing is selected.
  • remove_containers: remove the containers in docker_container_ids via docker rm (without -f, so Docker itself refuses to remove a still-running container)

docs.title: Git Built-in Workflows
docs.text: The Git plugin ships three workflows: one for commit creation and push automation, one for merging a branch into another one, and one for switching to another local branch.

docs.title: commit-ai
docs.text:
Creates a commit from the current working tree using an AI-generated commit message, then pushes it.

Source workflow: plugins/titan-plugin-git/titan_plugin_git/workflows/commit-ai.yaml

docs.title: Default flow
docs.text:
1. git.get_status
  2. before_commit hook
  3. git.show_uncommitted_diff_summary
  4. git.ai_generate_commit_message
  5. git.create_commit
  6. git.push

docs.title: Hooks
docs.text: • before_commit: inject validation or preparation steps before the commit is created

docs.title: Typical extension points
docs.text:
• run lints before committing
  • run tests before committing
  • collect extra project context before AI commit message generation

docs.title: Example extension
docs.text:
extends: "plugin:git/commit-ai"

hooks:
  before_commit:
    - id: lint
      name: "Run Ruff"
      command: "poetry run ruff check ."
      on_error: fail

docs.title: Related public steps
docs.text:
• get_status
  • show_uncommitted_diff_summary
  • ai_generate_commit_message
  • create_commit
  • push

docs.title: merge-branch
docs.text:
Merges another branch into the branch you are on, or into any other local branch via target_branch. When the merge conflicts, it hands the terminal to the configured interactive AI CLI so you can resolve the conflicts, then finishes the merge when you exit.

The merge never moves HEAD: the source branch is fetched and merged through its remote-tracking ref, so a failure at any point leaves you on the branch the merge lands on. The single exception is target_branch: resolve_merge_target checks that branch out, and only after everything that could refuse the merge has passed, so a refused merge still leaves you where you were.

Source workflow: plugins/titan-plugin-git/titan_plugin_git/workflows/merge-branch.yaml

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Param Default Meaning target_branch "" Branch the merge lands on. Empty means the one already checked out; anything else is checked out first. source_branch "" Branch to merge. Empty means the base branch configured for the project (plugins.git.main_branch). remote "origin" Remote the source branch is fetched from. merge_commit_no_verify true Skip pre-commit and commit-msg hooks on the merge commit. Deliberately not no_verify: that key is read by create_commit, and ctx.data is shared with workflows nested from the hooks.

docs.title: Default flow
docs.text:
1. before_merge hook
  2. git.resolve_merge_target (switches to target_branch when one is given)
  3. git.fetch_merge_source
  4. git.merge_source_branch
  5. core.ai_code_assistant (skips itself when there are no conflicts)
  6. git.complete_merge
  7. git.push (asks first; skips itself when there is nothing to push)
  8. after_merge hook

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
• Working tree must be clean. The workflow exits before touching anything if there are uncommitted changes. A merge on a dirty tree cannot be rolled back safely once it conflicts.
  • Merging into another branch. With target_branch set, the source branch, the dirty tree and "cannot merge a branch into itself" are all checked against that target before the checkout, so a merge that will not happen never moves you.
  • No conflicts: git commits the merge itself with the message it suggests. Steps 5 and 6 skip.
  • Conflicts: the conflicted files are listed, the AI CLI is launched with a prompt describing them, and on exit complete_merge runs git add --all plus a commit with git's prepared merge message.
  • Conflicts still unresolved on exit: you are asked whether to abort the merge (restoring the previous state) or commit as-is. "Unresolved" is decided by the file content, not by the index, so a file the AI CLI fixed without staging counts as resolved.
  • Pushing: the last step offers to push the branch, so the merge reaches the remote (and any PR on it) without a second workflow. It asks before pushing, skips itself when the branch has nothing unpushed, and never runs at all when the merge was aborted — an abort exits the workflow. Set confirm_push: false to push without asking.
  • Hooks on the merge commit: skipped by default (no_verify: true). The commit only carries git's own merge message, and a hook that fails at that point leaves the merge stopped with everything staged. Set no_verify: false to run them, or lint from the after_merge hook, where a failure no longer blocks the merge.

docs.title: Hooks
docs.text:
• before_merge: override source_branch or run pre-merge validation
  • after_merge: run anything that depends on the merge result, for example tests or a push

docs.title: Example: always merge develop
docs.text:
name: "Merge develop"

extends: "plugin:git/merge-branch"

params:
  source_branch: "develop"

docs.title: Example: run the project's own commit workflow after the merge
docs.text:
The merge commit itself always uses git's prepared merge message. Anything committed after the merge — an auto-corrected lint fix, a regenerated lockfile — is an ordinary commit, so route it through the project's commit workflow instead of duplicating commit logic here:

extends: "plugin:git/merge-branch"

hooks:
  after_merge:
    - id: verify
      name: "Verify the merged code"
      command: "./gradlew detekt --auto-correct"
      on_error: continue

    - id: commit_fixes
      name: "Commit fixes"
      workflow: "commit-ai"

Nested workflows resolve through the registry, so a commit-ai overridden in .titan/workflows/ wins over the plugin's version.

Two things to know before relying on this:

  • The nested commit workflow cannot double as the verification. commit-ai runs get_status first, before its before_commit hook, and get_status exits when the working tree is clean. After a successful merge commit the tree is clean, so the nested workflow exits at its first step and any lint injected in before_commit never runs. Put the verification in after_merge itself, as above.
  • The verification has to modify files for the commit step to do anything. A report-only linter leaves nothing to commit, so the nested workflow exits harmlessly. An Exit inside a nested workflow stops only that workflow, so the merge is unaffected either way.

Note that ctx.data is shared with nested workflows: a key set by merge-branch is visible to the steps of the workflow you nest.

  • fetch_merge_source
  • merge_source_branch
  • complete_merge

docs.title: switch-branch
docs.text:
Switches to another local branch. The branches you worked on most recently are offered first: the ones HEAD was switched to (from the reflog), then the rest by the date of their last commit, each one shown with how long ago that was and where it pushes.

The workflow refuses to move while the working tree has modified or staged files - those would travel to the other branch and mix with its work. Untracked files follow HEAD anywhere, so they never block it.

Source workflow: plugins/titan-plugin-git/titan_plugin_git/workflows/switch-branch.yaml

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Default Description branch "" Branch to switch to. Empty asks, offering the recently used ones. branch_limit 10 How many branches to offer.

docs.title: Default flow
docs.text: 1. git.switch_branch

docs.title: Example extension
docs.text:
extends: "plugin:git/switch-branch"

params:
  branch: "develop"

docs.title: Related public steps
docs.text: • switch_branch

docs.title: Git Client API
docs.text:
The Git plugin adds core Git operations to Titan through a high-level client and reusable workflows. It covers branches, commits, status inspection, diffs, remotes, stashes, tags, and worktrees.

This page documents the plugin from a functional point of view, while also showing how each capability is called and which parameters it needs.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
To use the Git plugin in a project:

  • Enable the git plugin in .titan/config.toml
  • Install the git CLI and make sure it is available in PATH
  • Run Titan inside a Git repository

Example project configuration:

[plugins.git]
enabled = true

[plugins.git.config]
main_branch = "main"
default_remote = "origin"

docs.title: Accessing the client
docs.text:
In Titan code, the public entry point is the Git plugin client:

git_plugin = config.registry.get_plugin("git")
client = git_plugin.get_client()

The client returns ClientResult[...] values. In practice, this means each call can succeed with data or return an error result.

docs.title: Get the current branch
docs.text:
Returns the currently checked out branch name.

Call:

client.get_current_branch()

Parameters:

  • No parameters.

docs.title: List branches
docs.text:
Returns local branches, or remote branches when requested.

Call:

client.get_branches(remote=False)

Parameters:

  • remote: Optional. Set to True to list remote branches instead of local ones.

docs.title: List recently used branches
docs.text:
Returns local branches ordered by how recently they were worked on: the branches HEAD was switched to come first (read from the reflog), then the rest by the date of their last commit. Each branch carries that date both raw (last_commit_date) and ready to show (formatted_date, e.g. "3 d").

Call:

client.list_recent_branches(limit=10, reflog_entries=300)

Parameters:

  • limit: Optional. Maximum number of branches to return.
  • reflog_entries: Optional. How far back in the reflog to look for checkouts.

docs.title: Create a branch
docs.text:
Creates a new branch from a starting point.

Call:

client.create_branch(branch_name="feature/search", start_point="HEAD")

Parameters:

  • branch_name: Required. New branch name.
  • start_point: Optional. Git ref to branch from.

docs.title: Create a branch and switch to it
docs.text:
Creates a branch and checks it out in one git checkout -b, so there is no state where the branch exists but is not checked out. Uncommitted work is carried over, as git always carries it to a branch starting at HEAD.

Call:

client.create_and_switch_branch(branch_name="feature/search", start_point="HEAD")

Parameters:

  • branch_name: Required. New branch name.
  • start_point: Optional. Git ref to branch from.

docs.title: Delete a branch
docs.text:
Deletes a branch directly.

Call:

client.delete_branch(branch="feature/search", force=False)

Parameters:

  • branch: Required. Branch name to delete.
  • force: Optional. Force deletion.

docs.title: Delete a branch safely
docs.text:
Deletes a branch only if it is not considered protected.

Call:

client.safe_delete_branch(branch="feature/search", force=False)

Parameters:

  • branch: Required. Branch name to delete.
  • force: Optional. Force deletion.

docs.title: Checkout a branch
docs.text:
Switches the repository to another branch.

Call:

client.checkout("feature/search")

Parameters:

  • branch: Required. Branch name to checkout.

docs.title: Check whether a branch exists on remote
docs.text:
Checks if a branch already exists in a remote repository.

Call:

client.branch_exists_on_remote(branch="feature/search", remote="origin")

Parameters:

  • branch: Required. Branch name.
  • remote: Optional. Remote name.

docs.title: Update a branch from remote
docs.text:
Fetches and fast-forwards a branch from the remote.

Call:

client.update_branch(branch="main", remote="origin")

Parameters:

  • branch: Required. Branch to update.
  • remote: Optional. Remote name. Defaults to the configured default remote.

docs.title: Update from the configured main branch
docs.text:
Updates the current branch from the configured main branch.

Call:

client.update_from_main()

Parameters:

  • No parameters.

docs.title: Checkout safely
docs.text:
Stores the current branch, optionally stashes local changes, and then switches branches.

Call:

client.safe_checkout(branch="feature/search", auto_stash=True)

Parameters:

  • branch: Required. Branch to checkout.
  • auto_stash: Optional. Automatically stash uncommitted changes first.

docs.title: Return to the original branch
docs.text:
Returns to the branch previously saved by safe_checkout.

Call:

client.return_to_original_branch()

Parameters:

  • No parameters.

docs.title: Check whether a branch is protected
docs.text:
Checks if a branch name is treated as protected by the client.

Call:

client.is_protected_branch("main")

Parameters:

  • branch: Required. Branch name.

docs.title: Create a commit
docs.text:
Creates a commit from the current working tree.

Call:

client.commit(message="feat: add search filters", all=False, no_verify=True)

Parameters:

  • message: Required. Commit message.
  • all: Optional. Include tracked modified files automatically.
  • no_verify: Optional. Skip Git hooks.

docs.title: Create a commit for specific files
docs.text:
Creates a commit only for the files passed in the call.

Call:

client.commit_files(
    files=["src/search.py", "tests/test_search.py"],
    message="test: cover search filters",
    no_verify=True,
)

Parameters:

  • files: Required. Files to include in the commit.
  • message: Required. Commit message.
  • no_verify: Optional. Skip Git hooks.

docs.title: Get the current commit SHA
docs.text:
Returns the SHA of HEAD.

Call:

client.get_current_commit()

Parameters:

  • No parameters.

docs.title: Get the commit SHA for a ref
docs.text:
Resolves any Git ref to its commit SHA.

Call:

client.get_commit_sha("HEAD~1")

Parameters:

  • ref: Required. Any Git ref.

docs.title: Get the merge base of two refs
docs.text:
Returns the SHA of the best common ancestor of two refs, the commit a pull request's diff is computed against.

Call:

client.get_merge_base("refs/titan/review/pr-236", "origin/master")

Parameters:

  • ref_a: Required. A Git ref.
  • ref_b: Required. A Git ref.

docs.title: Get a file as it is at a ref
docs.text:
Returns the content of a file at any ref without checking anything out, or None when the file does not exist at that ref (for example, a file a change adds). Content that is not text is returned as a ClientError.

Call:

client.get_file_at_ref("abc1234", "src/app/service.py")

Parameters:

  • ref: Required. A commit SHA, branch or tag.
  • path: Required. The repository-relative file path.

docs.title: Get commits versus base
docs.text:
Returns commit messages from the base branch up to HEAD.

Call:

client.get_commits_vs_base()

Parameters:

  • No parameters.

docs.title: Get commits in a branch compared to another branch
docs.text:
Returns the commits present in the head branch but not in the base branch.

Call:

client.get_branch_commits(base_branch="main", head_branch="feature/search")

Parameters:

  • base_branch: Required. Base branch.
  • head_branch: Required. Head branch.

docs.title: Get commits between refs
docs.text:
Returns commits reachable from one ref but not another.

Call:

client.get_commits_between_refs(base_ref="origin/main", head_ref="HEAD")

Parameters:

  • base_ref: Required. Base ref.
  • head_ref: Optional. Head ref.

docs.title: Count commits ahead of a base branch
docs.text:
Counts how many commits the current branch is ahead of another branch.

Call:

client.count_commits_ahead(base_branch="main")

Parameters:

  • base_branch: Optional. Base branch to compare against.

docs.title: Count unpushed commits
docs.text:
Counts how many commits have not been pushed to the remote yet.

Call:

client.count_unpushed_commits(branch=None, remote="origin")

Parameters:

  • branch: Optional. Branch to inspect. Uses the current branch when omitted.
  • remote: Optional. Remote name.

docs.title: Get repository status
docs.text:
Returns a structured view of the current repository state.

Call:

client.get_status()

Parameters:

  • No parameters.

Result: UIGitStatus with branch, is_clean, modified_files, untracked_files, staged_files, ahead, behind, has_upstream (False when the branch tracks nothing, so the counts are 0 for that reason), and the pre-formatted clean_icon, status_summary and sync_status.

docs.title: List untracked files
docs.text:
Returns every untracked file one by one, honouring .gitignore. Unlike get_status().untracked_files, a new directory is expanded into its files and ignored files (build output, __pycache__) are never listed.

Call:

client.get_untracked_files()

Parameters:

  • No parameters.

docs.title: Check for uncommitted changes
docs.text:
Returns whether the repository has local changes not yet committed.

Call:

client.has_uncommitted_changes()

Parameters:

  • No parameters.

docs.title: Get a diff between refs
docs.text:
Returns the diff between two refs.

Call:

client.get_diff(base_ref="origin/main", head_ref="HEAD")

Parameters:

  • base_ref: Required. Base ref.
  • head_ref: Optional. Head ref.

docs.title: Get the full uncommitted diff
docs.text:
Returns the diff of all local changes.

Call:

client.get_uncommitted_diff()

Parameters:

  • No parameters.

docs.title: Get the staged diff
docs.text:
Returns only the staged changes.

Call:

client.get_staged_diff()

Parameters:

  • No parameters.

docs.title: Get the unstaged diff
docs.text:
Returns only the unstaged changes.

Call:

client.get_unstaged_diff()

Parameters:

  • No parameters.

docs.title: Get the diff for one file
docs.text:
Returns the diff for a single file path.

Call:

client.get_file_diff("src/search.py")

Parameters:

  • file_path: Required. File path to inspect.

docs.title: Get the diff between branches
docs.text:
Returns the diff between two branches, with configurable context lines.

Call:

client.get_branch_diff(
    base_branch="main",
    head_branch="feature/search",
    context_lines=3,
    use_remote=False,
)

Parameters:

  • base_branch: Required. Base branch.
  • head_branch: Required. Head branch.
  • context_lines: Optional. Number of diff context lines.
  • use_remote: Optional. Treat both branches as remote refs.

docs.title: Get per-file change counters between branches
docs.text:
Returns a UIFileChurn list with exact additions/deletions per changed file (git diff --numstat). Binary files are included with is_binary=True and zero counters. Useful when an API source reports zeroed counters for files whose diff it cannot render.

Call:

client.get_branch_numstat(
    base_branch="main",
    head_branch="feature/search",
    use_remote=False,
)

Parameters:

  • base_branch: Required. Base branch.
  • head_branch: Required. Head branch.
  • use_remote: Optional. Treat both branches as remote refs.

docs.title: Get per-file counters of uncommitted changes
docs.text:
Returns one UIFileChurn per tracked file that differs from HEAD (working tree and index together), with additions, deletions and is_binary. It is read-only and safe to call repeatedly, e.g. from a timer. Prefer it over get_uncommitted_diff_stat(), which marks untracked files with intent-to-add as a side effect.

Call:

client.get_uncommitted_numstat(include_untracked=True)

Parameters:

  • include_untracked: Optional (default False). Also count new, untracked files (honouring .gitignore): each one's lines as additions; binary or unreadable files as is_binary=True with zero counters.

docs.title: List files changed between two refs
docs.text:
Returns the paths that differ between two refs (commits, branches or tags), one entry per path. Renames report both the old and the new path.

Call:

client.get_changed_files(base_ref="22aa7462", head_ref="4a999bc6")

Parameters:

  • base_ref: Required. Base ref, used verbatim (no remote prefixing).
  • head_ref: Required. Head ref, used verbatim.

docs.title: Get a diff stat between refs
docs.text:
Returns a summary of file-level changes between refs.

Call:

client.get_diff_stat(base_ref="origin/main", head_ref="HEAD")

Parameters:

  • base_ref: Required. Base ref.
  • head_ref: Optional. Head ref.

docs.title: Get the diff stat for uncommitted changes
docs.text:
Returns a compact summary of local changes.

Call:

client.get_uncommitted_diff_stat()

Parameters:

  • No parameters.

docs.title: Get the diff stat between branches
docs.text:
Returns a compact summary of changes between two branches.

Call:

client.get_branch_diff_stat(base_branch="main", head_branch="feature/search")

Parameters:

  • base_branch: Required. Base branch.
  • head_branch: Required. Head branch.

docs.title: Merge a ref into the current branch
docs.text:
Merges a ref into the checked out branch without opening an editor. A conflicted merge is not an error: the call returns ClientSuccess with a UIMergeResult whose status is MergeStatus.CONFLICTED and whose conflicted_files lists the unmerged paths, so the caller can drive conflict resolution.

Call:

client.merge(ref="origin/develop", target_branch="feature/search", no_ff=False)

Parameters:

  • ref: Required. Ref to merge, usually a remote-tracking ref such as origin/develop.
  • target_branch: Optional. Branch receiving the merge. Used for display only.
  • no_ff: Optional. Force a merge commit even when a fast-forward is possible.

Returns: ClientResult[UIMergeResult] with status in up_to_date, fast_forward, merged, conflicted.

docs.title: List conflicted files
docs.text:
Returns the paths git reports as unmerged in the index. Empty when the tree is clean.

Note that git keeps a path unmerged until it is staged, so a file whose conflict was already fixed in the editor still shows up here. Use List unresolved conflicts when you need to know whether the conflicts are actually gone.

Call:

client.get_conflicted_files()

Parameters: none.

docs.title: List unresolved conflicts
docs.text:
Returns only the unmerged paths whose working-tree content still contains conflict markers (<<<<<<< … >>>>>>>). Files that were resolved but not staged are excluded; paths that cannot be read (deleted or binary) are kept in the list so the caller can decide.

Call:

client.get_unresolved_conflict_files()

Parameters: none.

docs.title: List the conflicts between two refs
docs.text:
Returns the files that would conflict if base_ref were merged into head_ref, without touching the working tree, the index or HEAD: git merge-tree merges in memory, so this can be asked about a branch that is not checked out. An empty list means the merge would be clean. Requires git 2.38 or newer; an unknown ref (or an older git) comes back as a MERGE_TREE_FAILED error.

Remote-tracking refs are used as they are, so fetch first if the answer must be current.

Call:

client.list_merge_conflicts("origin/develop", "origin/feature/x")

Parameters:

  • base_ref: Required. Ref that would be merged in.
  • head_ref: Required. Ref receiving the merge.

docs.title: Check whether a merge is in progress
docs.text:
Returns True while MERGE_HEAD exists, that is, while a merge is stopped and waiting to be completed or aborted.

Call:

client.is_merge_in_progress()

Parameters: none.

docs.title: Stage every change
docs.text:
Stages the whole working tree, including untracked files. Used to mark conflicts as resolved before completing a merge.

Call:

client.stage_all()

Parameters: none.

docs.title: Complete an in-progress merge
docs.text:
Commits the staged merge using the message git prepared, without opening an editor.

Call:

client.continue_merge()
client.continue_merge(no_verify=False)

Parameters:

Parameter Required Default Description no_verify No True Skip pre-commit and commit-msg hooks. Skipping is the default because the commit only carries git's own merge message, and a hook that fails here leaves the merge stopped with everything staged.

Returns: ClientResult[str] with the merge commit SHA.

docs.title: Abort an in-progress merge
docs.text:
Restores the state from before the merge started.

Call:

client.abort_merge()

Parameters: none.

docs.title: Push to a remote
docs.text:
Pushes commits to a remote branch.

Call:

client.push(remote="origin", branch="feature/search", set_upstream=True, tags=False)

Parameters:

  • remote: Optional. Remote name.
  • branch: Optional. Branch to push. Uses the current branch when omitted.
  • set_upstream: Optional. Set the upstream tracking branch.
  • tags: Optional. Push tags too.

docs.title: Push a tag
docs.text:
Pushes a single tag to a remote.

Call:

client.push_tag(tag_name="v1.2.0", remote="origin")

Parameters:

  • tag_name: Required. Tag name.
  • remote: Optional. Remote name.

docs.title: Pull from a remote
docs.text:
Pulls changes from a remote branch.

Call:

client.pull(remote="origin", branch="main")

Parameters:

  • remote: Optional. Remote name.
  • branch: Optional. Branch to pull.

docs.title: Fetch from a remote
docs.text:
Fetches changes without merging them.

Call:

client.fetch(remote="origin", branch="main", all=False)

Parameters:

  • remote: Optional. Remote name.
  • branch: Optional. Branch to fetch.
  • all: Optional. Fetch all remotes.

docs.title: Extract GitHub repository info
docs.text:
Parses the remote URL and returns the GitHub owner and repository name when available.

Call:

client.get_github_repo_info()

Parameters:

  • No parameters.

docs.title: Create a stash
docs.text:
Stashes current local changes.

Call:

client.stash_push(message="temporary local changes")

Parameters:

  • message: Optional. Stash message.

docs.title: Pop a stash
docs.text:
Applies and removes a stash.

Call:

client.stash_pop(stash_ref=None)

Parameters:

  • stash_ref: Optional. Specific stash reference.

docs.title: Find a stash by message
docs.text:
Looks up a stash using its message.

Call:

client.find_stash_by_message("temporary local changes")

Parameters:

  • message: Required. Stash message to search for.

docs.title: Restore a stash by message
docs.text:
Finds a stash by message and restores it.

Call:

client.restore_stash("temporary local changes")

Parameters:

  • message: Required. Stash message to restore.

docs.title: Create a tag
docs.text:
Creates an annotated tag.

Call:

client.create_tag(tag_name="v1.2.0", message="Release 1.2.0", ref="HEAD")

Parameters:

  • tag_name: Required. Tag name.
  • message: Required. Tag annotation message.
  • ref: Optional. Ref to tag.

docs.title: Delete a tag
docs.text:
Deletes a local tag.

Call:

client.delete_tag("v1.2.0")

Parameters:

  • tag_name: Required. Tag name.

docs.title: Check whether a tag exists locally
docs.text:
Checks if a tag is present in the local repository.

Call:

client.tag_exists("v1.2.0")

Parameters:

  • tag_name: Required. Tag name.

docs.title: Check whether a tag exists on remote
docs.text:
Checks if a tag exists in a remote repository.

Call:

client.remote_tag_exists(tag_name="v1.2.0", remote="origin")

Parameters:

  • tag_name: Required. Tag name.
  • remote: Optional. Remote name.

docs.title: List tags
docs.text:
Returns the tags available in the repository.

Call:

client.list_tags()

Parameters:

  • No parameters.

docs.title: Create a worktree
docs.text:
Creates a new Git worktree.

Call:

client.create_worktree(
    path="../repo-search-worktree",
    branch="feature/search",
    create_branch=False,
    detached=False,
)

Parameters:

  • path: Required. Filesystem path for the worktree.
  • branch: Required. Branch to attach to the worktree.
  • create_branch: Optional. Create the branch if needed.
  • detached: Optional. Create the worktree in detached mode.

docs.title: Remove a worktree
docs.text:
Removes an existing worktree.

Call:

client.remove_worktree(path="../repo-search-worktree", force=False)

Parameters:

  • path: Required. Worktree path.
  • force: Optional. Force removal.

docs.title: Prune stale worktree metadata
docs.text:
Clears Git's records for worktrees whose directories no longer exist.

Git keeps administrative data under .git/worktrees for every registered worktree. If the directory is deleted by hand, or a removal is interrupted, that record survives and blocks the path: create_worktree reports it as already registered, while remove_worktree reports it as "not a working tree". Pruning is the only way to clear it, so call this before recreating a worktree at a path a previous run may have used.

Call:

client.prune_worktrees()

Parameters:

  • No parameters.

docs.title: List worktrees
docs.text:
Returns all worktrees for the repository.

Call:

client.list_worktrees()

Parameters:

  • No parameters.

docs.title: Run a Git command in a worktree
docs.text:
Runs a Git command inside a specific worktree.

Call:

client.run_in_worktree(worktree_path="../repo-search-worktree", args=["status", "--short"])

Parameters:

  • worktree_path: Required. Worktree path.
  • args: Required. Git arguments to execute.

docs.title: Get recent commits from a worktree
docs.text:
Returns recent commits from a specific worktree, in topological order (parents after their children).

Call:

client.get_commits(worktree_path="../repo-search-worktree", limit=10)
client.get_commits(worktree_path=".", limit=50, all_branches=True)

Parameters:

  • worktree_path: Required. Worktree path.
  • limit: Optional. Maximum number of commits.
  • all_branches: Optional. Walk every ref instead of HEAD only, as git log --all does.

Each UIGitCommit carries pr_number: the PR a squash merge landed, from the (#1234) GitHub appends to its subject (None otherwise). models.formatting.split_squash_pr_suffix(subject) returns the subject without it and the number.

It also carries parents (full hashes; more than one means a merge) and refs (the branches and tags pointing at it, with HEAD -> and tag: stripped). operations.build_commit_graph(commits) turns that list into UIGitGraphRows — the lane glyphs of a git log --graph drawing, one row per commit plus a link row wherever edges fork out — and operations.graph_lanes(rows) says how many columns they need.

docs.title: Get the worktree diff stat
docs.text:
Returns a diff summary for local changes in a worktree.

Call:

client.get_worktree_diff_stat(worktree_path="../repo-search-worktree")

Parameters:

  • worktree_path: Required. Worktree path.

docs.title: Checkout a branch in a worktree
docs.text:
Checks out, or creates, a branch inside a specific worktree.

Call:

client.checkout_branch_in_worktree(
    worktree_path="../repo-search-worktree",
    branch_name="feature/search",
    force=False,
)

Parameters:

  • worktree_path: Required. Worktree path.
  • branch_name: Required. Branch name.
  • force: Optional. Force the checkout.

docs.title: Commit changes in a worktree
docs.text:
Stages and commits changes inside a worktree.

Call:

client.commit_in_worktree(
    worktree_path="../repo-search-worktree",
    message="feat: add search filters",
    add_all=True,
    no_verify=False,
)

Parameters:

  • worktree_path: Required. Worktree path.
  • message: Required. Commit message.
  • add_all: Optional. Stage all tracked changes before committing.
  • no_verify: Optional. Skip Git hooks.

docs.title: Push from a worktree
docs.text:
Pushes a branch from a specific worktree to a remote.

Call:

client.push_from_worktree(
    worktree_path="../repo-search-worktree",
    branch="feature/search",
    remote="origin",
)

Parameters:

  • worktree_path: Required. Worktree path.
  • branch: Required. Branch to push.
  • remote: Optional. Remote name.

docs.title: Related workflows
docs.text:
The Git plugin ships with workflows that use these capabilities directly:

  • commit-ai: Checks repository status, shows a summary of local changes, generates a commit message with AI, creates the commit, and pushes it

These workflows can be used as-is or extended from .titan/workflows/.

docs.title: Git Plugin
docs.text:
The Git plugin provides Titan's core Git workflow surface. It exposes:

  • a high-level GitClient for direct use from Titan code
  • reusable workflow steps such as get_status, create_commit, and push
  • the built-in commit-ai and merge-branch workflows

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
To use the Git plugin in a project:

  • Enable the git plugin in .titan/config.toml
  • Install the git CLI and make sure it is available in PATH
  • Run Titan inside a Git repository

Example project configuration:

[plugins.git]
enabled = true

[plugins.git.config]
main_branch = "main"
default_remote = "origin"

docs.title: Public surfaces
docs.text:
• Client API: direct Python methods exposed by GitClient
  • Workflow Steps: public reusable workflow steps grouped by functionality
  • Built-in Workflows: workflows shipped by the plugin

docs.title: Mod
docs.text:
The plugin ships the git mod: a side-panel pane of three cards, read through GitClient on timers and refreshed after every workflow. Each card is a section you can switch off on the Mods screen.

  • repo — the current branch, its upstream, ahead/behind and the latest commits. The commits are drawn as a graph of every branch and tag, as gitk does (graph_all_branches; off, it follows only the current branch): one coloured lane per line of history, merges forking and closing as in git log --graph, with the branches and tags pointing at a commit beside its hash. A commit unfolds into its author, date, refs and Copy hash. While the history has more, ＋ Show more reads another recent_commits commits, and so on. Past graph_max_lanes lanes the graph would leave no room for the subject in a pane that narrow, so the card falls back to a plain list.
  • branches — the branch you are on at the top, and under it the branches you worked on most recently (reflog first, then last commit date), under a search field that is always there. Typing searches every branch a checkout reaches — local ones and remote ones with no local branch yet, marked · remote — and Enter switches to the branch the text names, exactly or as the only branch containing it; when several match, none does, or uncommitted work blocks the switch, it says so under the field and checks nothing out. A ✕ beside the field empties it, and a successful switch — from Enter or a row's Switch to it — empties it too. Any branch unfolds into Merge a branch into it…, a picker led by the project's configured base branch, which runs the merge workflow; the branch you are on also offers Pull origin/<branch>, Push origin/<branch> and Create PR, the others Switch to it. Create PR runs the create_pr_workflow (create-pr-ai from titan-plugin-github by default), or the project workflow extending it where the repo has one — the same run its menu entry opens — and shows only when this Titan has one of them; the commit and the push are that workflow's, so a dirty tree does not hide it. From the press until git answers, both buttons are replaced by a … pulling origin/<branch> line, so the card says what it is doing and a second press cannot start the same thing twice. A push git refuses is reported as git worded it, with the reason — the pane never forces one, since that would drop the remote's commits. The branch you are on also unfolds into New branch from it…: a field for the name, ✦ Suggest with AI — which reads the uncommitted diff under the prefixes this repo names its branches with (feat, fix, …, read from the branches themselves) and, where the github plugin is installed, the labels its pull requests carry — and Create <name> and switch, which is the only thing that creates anything: a suggestion just fills the field. The name is put in the shape git accepts and judged before git is asked, so a clash or a character git refuses is reported under the field. The new branch starts at the branch you are on and carries the uncommitted work with it, which is why the fold is offered with a dirty tree too — it is the way out of having worked on the wrong branch. While the working tree has modified or staged files the card turns amber, says so above everything and offers the commit workflow instead; the pull stays, since git decides for itself whether it is safe, and untracked files never block a switch.
  • worktrees — every worktree of the repository. One unfolds into its path and a two-press removal (the main worktree and the one Titan runs in are refused); a forced removal is offered only after git has refused one, and Prune stale records clears what git keeps for folders deleted by hand.

Options ([mods.git.options] in ~/.titan/config.toml): repo_refresh_seconds (30), branches_refresh_seconds (60), worktrees_refresh_seconds (120), refresh_key (f5, empty for none), recent_commits (10), graph_all_branches (on), graph_max_lanes (8), recent_branches (8), commit_workflow (commit-ai), create_pr_workflow (create-pr-ai), merge_workflow (merge-branch), suggestion_diff_chars (4000).

docs.title: Accessing the client
docs.text:
In Titan code, the public entry point is the Git plugin client:

git_plugin = config.registry.get_plugin("git")
client = git_plugin.get_client()

The client returns ClientResult[...] values. In practice, this means each call can succeed with data or return an error result.

docs.title: Public workflow steps
docs.text:
The Git plugin exposes these reusable public steps through get_steps():

  • get_status
  • create_commit
  • push
  • get_current_branch
  • get_base_branch
  • ai_generate_commit_message
  • show_uncommitted_diff_summary
  • show_branch_diff_summary
  • save_current_branch
  • restore_original_branch
  • checkout
  • pull
  • create_branch
  • resolve_merge_target
  • fetch_merge_source
  • merge_source_branch
  • complete_merge
  • create_worktree
  • remove_worktree
  • worktree_commit
  • worktree_push

These steps are intended for workflow authors. Their inputs, outputs, and return behavior are documented in Workflow Steps.

docs.title: Git Workflow Steps
docs.text:
The Git plugin exposes reusable public workflow steps through GitPlugin.get_steps(). These steps are grouped here by workflow intent so authors can discover related building blocks more easily.

For full contract details for every public step, including documented inputs, outputs, and return behavior, see the detailed step reference.

docs.title: Functional groups
docs.text:
• Status and Inspection
  • Commits
  • Branching
  • Merging
  • Diff Summaries
  • Worktrees

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: Step Group Used by built-in workflows get_status Status and Inspection commit-ai get_current_branch Status and Inspection create-pr-ai get_base_branch Status and Inspection - create_commit Commits commit-ai push Commits commit-ai, create-pr-ai, merge-branch ai_generate_commit_message Commits commit-ai save_current_branch Branching - restore_original_branch Branching - checkout Branching - switch_branch Branching switch-branch pull Branching - create_branch Branching - resolve_merge_target Merging merge-branch fetch_merge_source Merging merge-branch merge_source_branch Merging merge-branch complete_merge Merging merge-branch show_uncommitted_diff_summary Diff Summaries commit-ai show_branch_diff_summary Diff Summaries create-pr-ai create_worktree Worktrees - remove_worktree Worktrees - worktree_commit Worktrees - worktree_push Worktrees -

docs.title: Status and Inspection
docs.text:
Use these steps to inspect repository state and expose branch metadata to later steps.

  • get_status: retrieve repository status and expose git_status to the workflow context
  • get_current_branch: resolve the currently checked out branch name
  • get_base_branch: resolve the base branch used by Git workflows

docs.title: Commits
docs.text:
Use these steps to prepare commit content and publish branch changes.

  • create_commit: create a commit from workflow commit message data
  • push: push the current branch to the configured remote; set confirm_push: true to ask first
  • ai_generate_commit_message: generate a commit message from local changes using AI

docs.title: Branching
docs.text:
Use these steps to switch, create, and restore branches during a workflow.

  • save_current_branch: save the current branch in workflow context
  • restore_original_branch: restore the saved branch later in the workflow
  • checkout: switch to a branch from workflow context or params
  • switch_branch: pick one of the recently used branches and switch to it, refusing to move with uncommitted work
  • pull: update the current branch from the configured remote
  • create_branch: create a new branch from workflow-provided branch data

docs.title: Merging
docs.text:
Use these steps to integrate another branch into the current one. HEAD never moves: the source branch is fetched and merged through its remote-tracking ref.

  • resolve_merge_target: resolve the branch to merge and verify the working tree is clean
  • fetch_merge_source: fetch the source branch from the remote
  • merge_source_branch: run the merge and report conflicts as workflow data
  • complete_merge: stage resolved conflicts and commit with git's suggested message

docs.title: Diff Summaries
docs.text:
Use these steps when a workflow needs human-readable or AI-friendly summaries of Git changes.

  • show_uncommitted_diff_summary: summarize local uncommitted changes
  • show_branch_diff_summary: summarize branch-level changes relative to the base branch

docs.title: Worktrees
docs.text:
Use these steps to isolate workflow work in dedicated worktrees.

  • create_worktree: create a worktree for isolated work
  • remove_worktree: remove a worktree when finished
  • worktree_commit: commit changes inside a specific worktree
  • worktree_push: push a branch from a specific worktree

docs.title: Detailed Step Contracts
docs.text:
The summaries above show what each git step is for. The sections below show the documented contract for each public step: what it expects from ctx.data, what it saves back, and what result types it may return.

Expand a step to see its workflow usage, required context, inputs, outputs, and result behavior.

How to read these contracts:

  • Inputs (from ctx.data) = values the step expects before it runs.
  • Outputs (saved to ctx.data) = metadata keys saved for later steps when the step returns Success or Skip.
  • Returns = the workflow result type (Success, Skip, Error, Exit), not a separate payload.

docs.title: Docstring-based reference
docs.text:
The semiautomated step inventory reads public step docstrings from code and validates that each exposed step documents:

  • Requires
  • Inputs (from ctx.data) when applicable
  • Outputs (saved to ctx.data) when applicable
  • Returns

The generated machine-readable inventory lives under docs/plugins/_generated/.

For this project, the inventory is maintained through:

  • .titan/workflows/sync-plugin-docs.yaml
  • .titan/workflows/validate-plugin-docs.yaml
  • .titan/steps/sync_plugin_docs.py
  • .titan/steps/validate_plugin_docs.py

docs.title: GitHub Built-in Workflows
docs.text: The GitHub plugin ships reusable workflows for PR creation, issue creation, and PR comment response.

docs.title: create-pr-ai
docs.text:
Creates a pull request after preparing branch state, pushing changes, and generating PR content with AI.

Set params.draft to control draft behavior:

  • true: create as draft without prompting
  • false: create as ready for review without prompting
  • null: ask interactively before creating the PR

Source workflow: plugins/titan-plugin-github/titan_plugin_github/workflows/create-pr-ai.yaml

docs.title: Default flow
docs.text:
1. nested workflow commit-ai
  2. git.push
  3. git.get_current_branch
  4. git.show_branch_diff_summary
  5. before_pr_generation hook
  6. github.ai_suggest_pr_description
  7. github.prompt_for_pr_draft
  8. github.prompt_for_labels (configured to save into pr_labels)
  9. before_push hook
  10. github.create_pr
  11. after_pr hook

docs.title: Hooks
docs.text:
• before_pr_generation: inject project-specific context before AI generates PR content
  • before_push: run validations before PR creation
  • after_pr: notify or trigger post-creation automation

docs.title: create-issue-ai
docs.text:
Prompts for issue context, generates issue title and body with AI, then creates the GitHub issue.

Source workflow: plugins/titan-plugin-github/titan_plugin_github/workflows/create-issue-ai.yaml

docs.title: Default flow
docs.text:
1. github.prompt_for_issue_body_step
  2. github.ai_suggest_issue_title_and_body
  3. github.prompt_for_self_assign
  4. github.create_issue

docs.title: respond-pr-comments
docs.text:
Helps a contributor review pending PR comments, switch to the PR branch, apply changes, reply, and request another review.

Source workflow: plugins/titan-plugin-github/titan_plugin_github/workflows/respond-pr-comments.yaml

docs.title: Default flow
docs.text:
1. github.select_pr_for_review
  2. github.fetch_pending_comments
  3. github.check_clean_state
  4. github.checkout_pr_branch
  5. github.fetch_pr_review_bundle
  6. github.build_change_manifest
  7. github.judge_pr_comments
  8. github.review_comments
  9. after_review hook
  10. github.push_commits
  11. github.send_comment_replies
  12. github.request_review
  13. github.checkout_original_branch

docs.title: How a comment is judged
docs.text:
Before anything is asked of you, one AI session reads the whole PR and decides about every pending comment at once, and says for each one whether to change the code (apply), whether the branch already does it (already_done), whether the comment is mistaken (wrong), or whether it needs a human decision (needs_discussion) — with the files a fix would touch and the other places that use what would change.

That session reads the repository you are on, plus material Titan writes into .titan-review/ at its root (the diff per file, each file's version before the PR, the PR description and every comment). The directory is added to .git/info/exclude, so it stays out of git status and out of your commits — git commit -a never stages untracked files.

Each verdict is shown with its reasoning, and you decide: let the AI make the change, change it yourself, post the drafted reply (opened for editing first), write your own, or skip. When the session cannot run — AI off for the respond_pr_comment task, no CLI, a failed call — the comments are shown without verdicts and the workflow behaves as it did before.

An approved apply hands its verdict file to the interactive session that makes the change, so it starts with the callers and the risk already worked out instead of eleven lines of diff.

docs.title: What the run records
docs.text:
Every run writes what it did to ~/.titan/respond-comments/<repo>-pr<N>/runs/<run id>.json: one row per comment with its verdict, what you chose, whether that agreed with the verdict, and the commit it produced. The same facts go to the log as comment_decision and respond_comments_summary, next to comment_judgement_session and comment_judgement_summary (CLI, model, cost, duration). It is written to disk as well because logs rotate.

The point of the commit column: when a later review of the same PR reports a problem, git blame on that line gives a commit, and the record says which comment that commit was answering — so a fix that answered its comment and broke something else is traceable instead of being noticed by accident.

docs.title: Commit messages
docs.text:
Each fix is committed on its own. The subject line is written by AI from the diff that is about to be committed, with the comment thread handed over as the intent, and the body names the comment the commit answers and keeps the author attribution:

fix: Reject expired tokens before refreshing them

Addresses the review comment by @reviewer on src/auth.py:42.

By: reviewer

The subject is routed under the commit_message AI task, the same one the git plugin's "Commit with AI" uses, so one preference in AI Configuration covers both. With AI off for that task — or when no message can be generated — the commit falls back to Fix: <filename>.

docs.title: Hooks
docs.text: • after_review: run lints, tests, or other checks before pushing replies

docs.title: Example extension
docs.text:
extends: "plugin:github/respond-pr-comments"

hooks:
  after_review:
    - id: tests
      name: "Run Tests"
      command: "poetry run pytest"
      on_error: fail

docs.title: resolve-pr-conflicts
docs.text:
Un-conflicts one of your own pull requests: it checks out the PR's branch, merges the PR's base branch into it, hands the terminal to the interactive AI CLI to resolve the conflicts, offers to push so GitHub stops showing the PR as conflicting, and puts you back on the branch you started from.

The merge itself is plugin:git/merge-branch, run as a nested workflow rather than extended: a nested workflow's Exit — an aborted merge, nothing left to merge — comes back as Success, so the branch is restored either way. Extending it would let that Exit stop everything and leave you on the PR's branch.

Source workflow: plugins/titan-plugin-github/titan_plugin_github/workflows/resolve-pr-conflicts.yaml

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Param Default Meaning conflict_pr_number "" PR to un-conflict. Empty asks among your open PRs that GitHub reports as conflicting. The github mod's ⚒ Resolve conflicts button passes the PR it was pressed on. remote "origin" Remote the branches are fetched from.

docs.title: Default flow
docs.text:
1. github.select_conflicted_pr — picks the PR and lists the conflicting files, read with git merge-tree, which touches nothing
  2. github.check_clean_state — exits before anything is touched if the working tree is dirty
  3. github.checkout_pr_branch — saves the current branch and switches to the PR's
  4. plugin:git/merge-branch (nested), given the PR's base branch as source_branch: the merge, the interactive AI session on the conflicts, the merge commit, and the push it asks about
  5. github.checkout_original_branch — back to the branch you were on

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
• GitHub can lag: if the PR no longer conflicts by the time git is asked, the step says so and the merge proceeds as an ordinary one (or stops at "already up to date").
  • Declining the push leaves the merge committed on the PR's branch; it is pushed by whatever you do next on it.
  • Quitting the TUI mid-step unwinds the workflow with WorkflowAborted, and no later step runs: the branch is then left as it was at that moment.

docs.title: fix-pr-checks
docs.text:
Fixes the failing checks of one of your own pull requests: it reads the failed jobs' logs, checks out the PR's branch, opens an interactive AI session with those logs as its prompt, then offers to commit and push what the session changed, and puts you back on the branch you started from.

The pane's AI diagnosis says why a check failed; this is the other half, and the ✦ Fix with AI button there starts it with that diagnosis already in hand.

Source workflow: plugins/titan-plugin-github/titan_plugin_github/workflows/fix-pr-checks.yaml

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Param Default Meaning fix_pr_number "" PR to fix. Empty asks among your open PRs with a failing check. check_diagnosis "" What the pane already worked out, passed to the CLI as a hint it is told may be wrong. max_jobs 3 How many failed jobs' logs are read into the prompt. The rest are named, not read.

docs.title: Default flow
docs.text:
1. github.select_failing_pr — picks the PR, reads the failed jobs' logs and builds check_fix_context
  2. github.check_clean_state — exits before anything is touched if the working tree is dirty
  3. github.checkout_pr_branch — saves the current branch and switches to the PR's
  4. core.ai_code_assistant — the interactive session, on the PR's branch, with the logs as its prompt
  5. plugin:git/commit-ai (nested) — commits what changed with an AI message and pushes it; nested so that "nothing to commit" does not stop the workflow
  6. github.checkout_original_branch — back to the branch you were on

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
• The CLI is told not to commit: the prompt asks it to fix and verify, and leaves committing to step 5, where you see the diff and the message first.
  • External CI: a failed check that is not a GitHub Actions job has no log to read, so only its name reaches the prompt.
  • Checks already green: if the PR has no failing check by the time it is asked, the workflow says so and exits.

docs.title: GitHub Client API
docs.text:
The GitHub plugin adds GitHub operations to Titan through a high-level client and reusable workflows. It covers pull requests, reviews, issues, releases, teams, and repository metadata.

This page documents the plugin from a functional point of view, while also showing how each capability is called and which parameters it needs.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
To use the GitHub plugin in a project:

  • Enable the github plugin in .titan/config.toml
  • Enable the git plugin, because the GitHub plugin depends on it
  • Use a GitHub repository that is either configured explicitly or detectable from the git remote
  • Install and authenticate the gh CLI

Example project configuration:

[plugins.git]
enabled = true

[plugins.github]
enabled = true

[plugins.github.config]
repo_owner = "example-org"
repo_name = "example-repo"
default_branch = "main"
pr_template_path = ".github/pull_request_template.md"
auto_assign_prs = true

docs.title: Accessing the client
docs.text:
In Titan code, the public entry point is the GitHub plugin client:

github_plugin = config.registry.get_plugin("github")
client = github_plugin.get_client()

The client returns ClientResult[...] values. In practice, this means each call can succeed with data or return an error result.

docs.title: Create a pull request
docs.text:
Creates a new pull request from a head branch into a base branch.

Call:

client.create_pull_request(
    title="Add search filters",
    body="## Summary\n- adds filter controls\n- updates results state",
    base="main",
    head="feature/search-filters",
    draft=False,
    assignees=["alice"],
    reviewers=["bob", "example-org/backend-team"],
    labels=["feature", "ui"],
    excluded_reviewers=["carol"],
)

Parameters:

  • title: Required. Pull request title.
  • body: Required. Pull request description.
  • base: Required. Target branch.
  • head: Required. Source branch.
  • draft: Optional. Whether to create the PR as draft.
  • assignees: Optional. GitHub usernames to assign.
  • reviewers: Optional. Usernames or teams.
  • labels: Optional. Labels to apply.
  • excluded_reviewers: Optional. Usernames to exclude after team expansion.

docs.title: Get a pull request
docs.text:
Fetches a single pull request by number.

Call:

client.get_pull_request(123)

Parameters:

  • pr_number: Required. Pull request number.

Returns:

A UIPullRequest object with the following fields:

  • number: PR number
  • title: PR title
  • body: PR description
  • status_icon: Status emoji (🟢 open, 🔴 closed, 🟣 merged, 📝 draft)
  • state: PR state (OPEN, CLOSED, MERGED)
  • author_name: GitHub username of PR author
  • head_ref: Source branch name
  • base_ref: Target branch name
  • branch_info: Formatted branch information (e.g., "feature/xyz → main")
  • stats: Formatted change statistics (e.g., "+123 -45")
  • additions / deletions: The same counts as numbers, for a UI that colours them apart
  • files_changed: Number of files changed
  • is_mergeable: Whether the PR can be merged
  • is_draft: Whether the PR is a draft
  • review_summary: Formatted review status (e.g., "✅ 2 approved")
  • labels: List of label names
  • requested_reviewers: GitHub usernames of all users requested to review
  • pending_reviewers: GitHub usernames of users who haven't reviewed yet
  • reviewers: UIReviewer(login, state, icon, when) per person involved, the ones who block the PR first and the ones still pending last. state is "changes_requested", "approved", "commented" or "pending"; icon is ✗ ✓ ✎ ○; when is how long ago they reviewed ("2d ago", empty while pending); has_reviewed says whether request_pr_review can ask them again. A reviewer asked again after reviewing counts as pending, as GitHub shows them, and a requested team is named by its slug. Filled by list_my_prs.
  • assignees: GitHub usernames assigned to the PR. Filled by list_my_prs and list_my_involved_prs.
  • opened_age / updated_age: How long ago the PR was opened and last touched ("5d ago")
  • checks_summary: Compact check counts (e.g., "2 failing, 5 passing")
  • review_status_summary: "approved", "changes requested", "review required" or "draft"
  • checks_state: One state for all checks: "failing", "running", "passing" or "none" (check runs and external commit statuses alike)
  • failed_checks: UIFailedCheck(name, url, job_id) for each failed check, url being the Actions job page or the external CI's link, job_id the Actions job id to pass to get_actions_job_log (None for external CI), run_id the Actions run id to pass to rerun_failed_jobs
  • url: The PR's web page
  • has_conflicts: True when GitHub reports the PR as conflicting.

The three list methods read the same repository listing and ask GitHub for the same fields, so a PR carries the same data whichever one returned it. stats, files_changed, opened_age and updated_age are not part of a listing and stay empty until get_pull_request fills them.

docs.title: List pull requests pending review
docs.text:
Returns the open PRs with a review request standing for you.

Call:

client.list_pending_review_prs(max_results=25)

Parameters:

  • max_results: Optional. Maximum number of PRs to return.

Only requests addressed to you personally: GitHub also lists the teams asked to review, and whether you are in one of them is not part of the PR.

docs.title: List your pull requests
docs.text:
Returns pull requests created by the authenticated user.

Call:

client.list_my_prs(state="open", max_results=25)

Parameters:

  • state: Optional. PR state such as open, closed, or merged.
  • max_results: Optional. Maximum number of PRs to return.

docs.title: List pull requests you opened or are assigned to
docs.text:
Returns pull requests created by the authenticated user plus those assigned to them. Used by respond-pr-comments, so anyone who self-assigns a PR can answer its comments.

Call:

client.list_my_involved_prs(state="open", max_results=25)

Parameters:

  • state: Optional. PR state such as open, closed, or merged.
  • max_results: Optional. Maximum number of PRs to return.

docs.title: How the filtered lists are built
docs.text: list_pending_review_prs, list_my_prs and list_my_involved_prs list the repository and pick from the result; they never query GitHub's search index. An organization can keep its repositories out of that index, and a search that cannot see them answers nothing rather than failing, so a search-backed list is empty and no error is raised — indistinguishable from having no PRs. Because the filtering happens here, both read deeper than they return (at least 200 PRs), so yours are not hidden behind other people's in a busy repository.

docs.title: List all pull requests
docs.text:
Returns pull requests from the repository without filtering by author.

Call:

client.list_all_prs(state="open", max_results=50)

Parameters:

  • state: Optional. PR state such as open, closed, or merged.
  • max_results: Optional. Maximum number of PRs to return.

docs.title: Search pull requests
docs.text:
Searches the repository's PRs with GitHub's own search syntax, the same text its PR search box takes.

Call:

client.search_prs("author:ana label:bug review:approved", state="open", max_results=30)

Parameters:

  • query: Required. Free text and qualifiers: author:, label:, review:, status:, draft:, base:, head:… An empty query is the plain repository listing (list_all_prs).
  • state: Optional. open (default), closed, merged or all.
  • max_results: Optional. Maximum number of PRs (default 30).

Result: ClientSuccess with a list of UIPullRequest, as every other listing returns them. ClientError (API_ERROR) with GitHub's reason otherwise, such as a rate limit. Unlike the listings above it uses GitHub's search API, which has a limit of its own (30 requests a minute), so call it for a search the person asked for and not on a timer.

docs.title: Count open pull requests
docs.text:
Returns how many pull requests are open in the repository, in one GraphQL call, without listing them (no cap, unlike len(list_all_prs(...))).

Call:

client.count_open_prs()

Parameters: none. GRAPHQL_UNAVAILABLE when the client has no GraphQL network.

docs.title: Get the repository name
docs.text:
Returns the repository this client works on, as "owner/name". No network call.

Call:

client.get_repo_full_name()  # "masorange/titan-cli"

Parameters: none.

docs.title: Read a pull request diff
docs.text:
Returns the pull request diff as text.

Call:

client.get_pr_diff(pr_number=123, context_lines=3)

Parameters:

docs.title: Read patches for specific files
docs.text:
Returns patch text only for selected files in a PR.

Call:

client.get_pr_file_patches(123, ["src/search.py", "tests/test_search.py"])

Parameters:

  • pr_number: Required. Pull request number.
  • file_paths: Required. List of paths to extract patches for.

docs.title: List changed files
docs.text:
Returns the file paths changed in a pull request.

Call:

client.get_pr_files(123)

Parameters:

  • pr_number: Required. Pull request number.

docs.title: List changed files with stats
docs.text:
Returns each changed file together with additions, deletions, and status.

Call:

client.get_pr_files_with_stats(123)

Parameters:

docs.title: Checkout a pull request locally
docs.text:
Checks out the pull request branch in the local repository.

client.checkout_pr(123)

docs.title: Add a PR comment
docs.text:
Adds a general comment to a pull request.

client.add_comment(123, "Please add test coverage for the empty state.")

Parameters:

docs.title: Get the PR head commit SHA
docs.text:
Returns the pull request's head commit SHA (headRefOid). Reliable regardless of how many commits the PR has — it does not depend on the commit list, which the gh CLI truncates at 100 entries.

client.get_pr_commit_sha(123)

Parameters:

docs.text:
Returns compact remote context for a commit SHA mentioned in review discussion, including changed files and a truncated patch excerpt suitable for AI prompts.

Call:

client.get_commit_review_context(

Parameters:

  • max_patch_chars: Optional. Maximum combined patch excerpt size before truncation.

docs.title: Merge a pull request
docs.text:
Merges a pull request using the selected merge strategy, or adds it to the base branch's merge queue when that branch requires one.

Call:

client.merge_pr(
    pr_number=123,
    merge_method="squash",
    commit_title="Add search filters",
    commit_message="Adds filtering controls and updates result handling.",
)

Parameters:

  • pr_number: Required. Pull request number.
  • merge_method: Optional. Merge strategy such as merge, squash, or rebase. Ignored when the base branch requires a merge queue: the queue owns the strategy.
  • commit_title: Optional. Merge commit title. Ignored for a queued pull request.
  • commit_message: Optional. Merge commit message. Ignored for a queued pull request.
  • merge_queue_enabled: Optional. Known merge queue state, to skip the detection lookup (for example the merge_queue_enabled value produced by the check_merge_queue step). When omitted the state is detected automatically; a detection that fails falls back to a regular merge and appends a "merge queue detection failed" note to the result message, so a rejection by a queue-protected branch is not mistaken for a plain merge failure.

Result: UIPRMergeResult. A queued pull request comes back with merged=False, queued=True and the queue_position GitHub assigned it. It is neither a merge nor a failure: GitHub merges it when the queue clears.

Queueing goes through GraphQL, so it needs a client with a GraphQL network configured. A regular merge does not. Without one, a pull request whose base branch requires a queue comes back with merged=False and queued=False rather than being merged directly.

docs.title: Re-run failed jobs
docs.text:
Re-runs the failed and cancelled jobs of a GitHub Actions workflow run; jobs that passed are not run again. GitHub only accepts it once the whole run has finished.

Call:

client.rerun_failed_jobs(run_id=123456789)

Parameters:

  • run_id: Required. Workflow run id (UIFailedCheck.run_id).

Result: ClientSuccess once GitHub has queued the re-run; ClientError (API_ERROR) with GitHub's reason otherwise, e.g. the run is still in progress.

docs.title: List workflow runs
docs.text:
Lists the repository's latest GitHub Actions runs, newest first, whoever started them.

Call:

client.list_workflow_runs(trigger="merge_group", limit=10, page=1)

Parameters:

  • trigger: Optional. Only runs started by this event ("pull_request", "push", "merge_group"…). "merge_group" gives the merge queue's own runs. Default: every event.
  • limit: Optional. Runs per page, 1 to 100 (default 10).
  • page: Optional. 1-based page, to read further back (default 1).

Result: ClientSuccess with a list of UIWorkflowRun: id, number, title (what GitHub shows: the PR title, "Merge group checks requested"…), workflow, event, state ("running", "success", "failure", "cancelled" or "other") and a readable state_label, branch, url, age ("4m ago"), duration ("2m 56s", empty while it runs) and actor. A merge queue run (is_merge_queue) also has pr_number, read from its branch gh-readonly-queue/<base>/pr-<number>-<sha>. ClientError (API_ERROR) otherwise.

docs.title: Get the failed jobs of a workflow run
docs.text:
Returns the jobs of a run that failed, timed out or were cancelled, so their logs can be read (see Get the log of a GitHub Actions job).

Call:

client.get_run_failed_jobs(run_id=123456789)

Parameters:

  • run_id: Required. Workflow run id (UIWorkflowRun.id).

Result: ClientSuccess with a list of UIFailedCheck, each with the job_id its log is read by and the run's id as run_id; empty when every job passed. ClientError (API_ERROR) otherwise.

docs.title: Re-run a workflow run
docs.text:
Re-runs every job of a finished GitHub Actions workflow run, the ones that passed too. To re-run only what failed use Re-run failed jobs. GitHub only accepts it once the whole run has finished.

Call:

client.rerun_workflow(run_id=123456789)

Parameters:

  • run_id: Required. Workflow run id (UIWorkflowRun.id).

Result: ClientSuccess once GitHub has queued the re-run; ClientError (API_ERROR) with GitHub's reason otherwise, e.g. the run is still in progress.

docs.title: Get the merge queue state of a pull request
docs.text:
Returns whether the base branch requires a merge queue and whether the pull request is currently queued. These fields are only available through GraphQL, so they are not part of get_pull_request.

Call:

client.get_merge_queue_state(pr_number=123)

Parameters:

  • pr_number: Required. Pull request number.

Result: UIMergeQueueState with is_merge_queue_enabled, is_in_merge_queue, pr_state, queue_position, queue_entry_state and a pre-formatted summary.

docs.title: Get the log of a GitHub Actions job
docs.text:
Returns the end of one Actions job's log, e.g. to explain a failed check. The job id comes with each failed check (UIFailedCheck.job_id); checks reported by external CI have none and no Actions log. To explain the failure with an AI, see operations/ci_diagnosis_operations.py: extract_failure_excerpt(log), build_job_diagnosis_prompt(job_name, excerpt) → (prompt, system), parse_job_diagnosis(job_name, answer, excerpt) → UIJobDiagnosis (cause, where, quote, is_quote_in_log) and format_job_diagnoses(...) for a plain-text report.

Call:

client.get_actions_job_log(job_id=51234567890, tail_chars=3_000_000)

Parameters:

  • job_id: Required. GitHub Actions job id.
  • tail_chars: Optional. How many characters from the end of the log to keep (default 3,000,000); a failure is reported at the end of the log.

Result: the log text, timestamps included. JOB_NOT_FOUND when the job does not exist or its log has expired.

docs.title: Get the merge queue
docs.text:
Returns the whole merge queue of the repository's default branch, read-only. A repository without a merge queue is a success with is_configured=False.

Call:

client.get_merge_queue(max_entries=8)

Parameters:

  • max_entries: Optional. How many entries to list from the head of the queue (default 10); total always counts the whole queue.

Result: UIMergeQueue with is_configured, branch, merge_method, total and entries. Each UIMergeQueueEntry carries position, pr_number, title, author, state, a readable state_label ("running checks", "ready to merge"…), eta_seconds, a compact eta_label ("~12m"), is_mine for the authenticated user's own pull requests, the PR's url, queued_age ("12m ago") and checks_state of the queue's merge commit ("passing", "failing", "running" or ""). UIMergeQueue.next_eta_label is GitHub's estimate for the head of the queue.

docs.title: Get review threads

client.create_release(

docs.text: Browse a repository's file tree through the GitHub Contents API, without cloning it locally. Both methods default to the client's own configured repo, but accept repo_owner/repo_name to read from a different repository.

client.list_repository_directory(

Returns a ClientResult[List[dict]]. Each entry is shaped like {"name": str, "path": str, "type": "dir" | "file"}. Returns ClientError (NOT_A_DIRECTORY) if path points to a file instead of a directory, and ClientError (NOT_FOUND) if the path doesn't exist.
